workflows.title: MOSS-Image SFT text to image (plain words or a layout of boxes; strong Chinese and English text)
workflows.license: Apache-2.0 (MOSS-Image SFT and Base, Qwen3.5-9B, FLUX.2 small decoder, byte-identical to BFL's Apache-2.0 FLUX.2-small-decoder; Fast: Spectrallic's MOSS-Image SFT 8-step DMD int8 file, Apache-2.0)
workflows.notes: Core nodes only (MOSS-Image is native in the pinned ComfyUI): Comfy-Org's template image_moss_image_t2i_bboxes without its subgraph, TextGenerate upsampler and box nodes. The prompt is plain words or a compiled layout (a summary + items with pixel boxes from the canvas centre, y before x), which reaches the model verbatim; width / height are the layout's canvas (multiples of 16, up to 2048). Standard = the template: 25 steps, CFG 2.5, er_sde / simple, skip-layer guidance on layer 22 for the first half; Quality = the MOSS-Image user guide: 50 steps, CFG 3, euler; Fast = Spectrallic's SFT with the 8-step DMD LoRA merged (unet), 8 steps, CFG 1; Base = MOSS-Image Base (unet) at 50 steps, CFG 3, euler. The text encoder is qwen3.5_9b_int8_convrot (the int8 file FIBO 2's prompt writer also loads), not the template's qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq. The 16 GB VRAM figure is an estimate, as MOSS-Image publishes none: about 15 GB of files (DiT 5.4 + encoder 9.7 + VAE 0.25), and ComfyUI offloads. The int8 files run through comfy-kitchen's kernels, which need a PyTorch built for CUDA 13 (cu130): comfy/quant_ops.py turns its CUDA backend off otherwise and logs a warning, and the model may run slower.

workflows.notes: Comfy-Org's image_flux3_klein_distilled_t2i (2026-10-15, minComfyUIVersion 0.41.0) without its subgraph, ResolutionSelector, box editor and notes; core nodes only. The prompt goes to TextGenerate on BFL's FLUX 3 prompt upsampler (CLIPLoader type flux3, 3,584 tokens, top_k 1 as the card's greedy decoding, presence penalty 1.5, the t2i system prompt of black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup@3f3edb52), whose caption Qwen3-VL-4B encodes. Prompt helper off (params.extra.promptHelper "off"), or a layout of boxes (compileFlux3: a caption citing <obj_N>, then the 0-1000 table), sends the words as typed: the provider takes the helper's branch out. Distilled: 16 steps (the card; the template has 15), CFG 1, er_sde / simple, an empty negative. The template's file names (flux3_image_klein_sd_int8_convrot) are not in the repository: the files are BFL's (flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot). VRAM about 16-24 GB, estimated: BFL's card gives 25-31 GB on a B200 at 1 MP with the helper off, Freefield measured 17.8 GB with the int8 files; the helper adds a 6.7 GB encoder, which ComfyUI offloads after it runs.

workflows.title: Restore an old or damaged photo, same faces and framing (Qwen-Image 2.1 + AusBoss Restore LoRA, then SeedVR2 2x)
workflows.license: Qwen Research License Agreement (Qwen-Image 2.1): NON-COMMERCIAL, research and evaluation only; Restore LoRA by AusBoss under the same licence; SeedVR2 Apache-2.0
workflows.notes: One restore pass as the Restore LoRA card sets it up, then a SeedVR2 enlargement. The photo is scaled to about 2 MP on the 32 grid (ImageScaleToTotalPixels, lanczos: small prints grow to it, big noisy ones shrink to it, as the card asks) -> UNETLoader -> LoraLoaderModelOnly (qwen-image-2.1-restore, step 1,500; loraStrength 1.0, 0.5 for a blurry photo) -> QwenImage21Cache -> TextEncodeQwenImage21 (the photo as image 1, resolution 0, no negative) -> KSampler on its latent, 25 steps, cfg 1, euler, simple, denoise 1 -> VAEDecode -> SplitImageWithAlpha. Then SeedVR2 7B int8 one step (the nodes of the upscale-image-seedvr2 template): ResizeImageMaskNode x scale (2) lanczos -> Preprocess -> VAEEncodeTiled 512/128 -> Conditioning -> KSampler 1 step -> VAEDecodeTiled -> PostProcessing (lab colour from the restored photo). About 8 MP out. Prompt: one of the two instructions the LoRA was trained on, alone (a wrong "Scene:" description painted features that were not there). No turbo LoRA (25 steps sat closer: 0.15 px, face 0.90). One pass only (a second came back crunchy); never with the Consistency or Outfit-Swap LoRA. Faces under about 100 px can come back as a slightly different person. The open route of the Restore Photo app. RTX 5090: about 70 s a photo at 25 steps, peak about 31 GB.

workflows.title: Keyframe animation: Wan 2.2 14B first/last-frame in-betweens with AniSora 3.2, every Nth frame per gap, one video
workflows.license: Apache-2.0 (Wan 2.2 I2V A14B, lightx2v 4-step LoRA, bilibili Index-AniSora V3.2; Kijai's AniSora extraction states no licence of its own)
workflows.notes: One Wan 2.2 FLF2V pass per pair of neighbouring keyframes, all sharing one set of loaders: the high-noise expert with AniSora 3.2 (strength 1) and the low-noise expert with the lightx2v 4-step LoRA (strength 1), ModelSamplingSD3 shift 5 on both, KSamplerAdvanced 4 steps at CFG 1, euler / simple, high 0-2 with leftover noise, low 2-end; umt5 fp8, Wan 2.1 VAE, Wan's standard negative words. Each pass has its own length (4n + 1, 17-81 frames), words and seed. VHS_SelectEveryNthImage keeps every Nth frame (1-4) counted back from the next keyframe (skip_first_images = ((length - 2) mod N) + 1), so each pose is on screen and no joint shows a frame twice; keyframe 1 (ImageFromBatch of pass 1) goes in front; BatchImagesNode joins them in order and CreateVideo plays them at 24 fps (snappier, the passes are made at 16 fps) or 16 fps (true time). About 24 GB of VRAM at 720p; RAM for the decoded frames grows with the total length.

workflows.notes: Text to video with sound: MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo with no frames given, the fl2va pruned int8 model with the turbo v4 LoRA at 1.0 (MiniMaxH3TurboLoRA, MiniMaxH3TurboSampler), BasicScheduler simple 8 steps, H3SLAAttention (sparsity 0.85, block 64, int8 QK; needs Triton) and H3AdaLNLoRAFix (port), CFG 1. workflows.title: Edit what was said with Tencent AuK (words, pitch, pace, emotion, noise; windows crossfaded back)
workflows.license: AuK code and weights MIT (Tencent); its Qwen2.5-Omni-3B encoder Qwen Research License (NON-COMMERCIAL)
workflows.notes: The recording (a video upload works: LoadAudio reads its soundtrack) and the edit windows Fuobe plans (params.extra.speechWindows: start, end, instruction, seconds). The graph is rebuilt for every window in one prompt: each window is cut with TrimAudioDuration, edited by AuKGenerateEdit (one shared AuKModelLoader) and crossfaded back over its first and last 0.12 s as a + (b − a) × fade-in, with the linear fade-in Fuobe writes (fadeCurve: the ramp, then a flat tail AudioMerge trims off). The recording and each edit are first brought to one rate (merged with silence at the other's: AuK speaks at 24 kHz), so no seam piece is resampled at its edges (a resampled piece tapers there: a click). Windows hold at least 1 s of untouched speech each side and are cut at silences. AuK takes a window plus its new audio up to 30 s per call (its node refuses more and does not split), so a window is at most about 14.7 s for a same-length effect. AuK-Flash by default (checkpoint ckpts/AuK-Flash/auk_flash.safetensors, 4 steps, CFG 0, sway -1); params.extra.quality "best" loads ckpts/AuK/auk_base.safetensors at 32 steps, CFG 2. The Prompt Enhancer is off: Fuobe writes the Cookbook instruction (Replace 'X' with 'Y'. / Add … after … / Remove …; pitch, speed, volume, emotion, whisper, enhancement and speaker extraction) and sets generation_seconds itself. device is bound to the server's first torch device (cuda:0, or cpu with fp32). workflows.title: Find watermarks, captions, logos, stickers and mosaics on a photo (Qwen3-VL, ComfyUI-Qwen-Watermark)
workflows.license: Qwen3-VL 8B Apache-2.0; ComfyUI-Qwen-Watermark nodes MIT
workflows.notes: The pack's detect-only workflow (qwen_watermark_detection.api.json) without its preview and save nodes: QWMDetect auto_qwen reads the picture once with Qwen3-VL 8B (int8, detection side 1536, up to 2048 tokens, expand 20, padding 0.35, min confidence 0.65) and PreviewAny shows its report: JSON {coordinate_space: "pixels", image_size, boxes: [{label, bbox (padded repair box), source_bbox (tight), overlay_type, mask_method, confidence}], rejected_boxes (below 0.65), status}. Four more QWMDetect read the photo in quarters (ImageCrop, each 4/7 of the width and height from GetImageSize and ComfyMathExpression a * 4 // 7, so a mark repeated over the photo comes back copy by copy); their reports (role scan-tile) are merged into the report by the provider (mergeScanReports). The app draws source_bbox and sends the kept boxes to image-watermark-remove-qwen21. The GPU pre-flight also checks image-watermark-remove-qwen21 for a scan (its companion graph).

workflows.title: Remove watermarks, captions, logos, stickers and mosaics, the rest unchanged (Qwen-Image 2.1, ComfyUI-Qwen-Watermark)
workflows.license: Qwen Research License Agreement (Qwen-Image 2.1): NON-COMMERCIAL, research and evaluation only; Qwen3-VL 8B Apache-2.0; SAM ViT-B (segment-anything) Apache-2.0; ComfyUI-Qwen-Watermark nodes MIT
workflows.notes: The pack's main workflow (qwen21_watermark.api.json, plain settings) with the int8 UNET (qwen_image_2.1_int8_convrot, as Live edit) and without its debug save and preview nodes. QWMDetect (manual_boxes with the kept boxes and a 32 px repair margin past the scan's box; auto_qwen with expand 20 for API callers) -> QWMRefineMask (a rectangle for text, logos, blocks and mosaics, a SAM ViT-B outline for stickers) -> QWMPrepare (context 96, max side maxSize, no pre-fill: the OpenCV pre-fill smeared the pattern of a mosaic into a large box) -> Qwen-Image 2.1 edit, 20 steps, cfg 1 -> QWMComposite (feather 6, align, colour match) -> QWMResidualDetect (Qwen3-VL looks for leftovers inside the first mask) -> one more pass when it finds some -> QWMFinal keeps the better pass and raises when any pixel outside the mask changed. Outputs: the picture (SaveImage, PNG) and the quality report (PreviewAny, role quality: folded into the picture's meta, never a result of its own). Seeds are random per run. The structure settings (denoise 0.65 / 0.55, context 384, no pre-fill) are the pack's alternative for faces.

workflows.title: Qwen-Image 2.1 Recolor (tap mask by name, crop, repaint, paste back)
workflows.license: Qwen Research License Agreement (Qwen-Image 2.1): NON-COMMERCIAL, research and evaluation only; Meta SAM License (SAM 3.1); AusBoss nodes MIT
workflows.notes: Tap to Recolor: qwen-image-21-inpaint with the mask made in the graph from the taps by AusBoss Mask by Touch on core SAM 3.1. touches = the node's JSON {"v":1,"items":[{"t":"name","w":word,"x":int,"y":int,"op":1|0}]} in the photo's pixels: each tap asks for the smallest thing of the piece's name under it (Jacket: jacket + clothing; Auto: clothing, bag, shoe, hat, scarf), a Leave out tap takes away a hand, arm, hair, belt, bag strap or necklace under it. SAM 3.1's point prompt alone (SAM3_Detect) returned the whole person on every GPU test, so taps go through names. If nothing is found the mask is empty and the photo comes back unchanged (if_nothing "empty mask"); free_vram unloads SAM before the repaint. -> GrowMask maskGrow (1) -> Crop For Inpaint (context 1.4, blend 2 px, multiple 32, 1.5 MP, bicubic: a tight paste, since a wider one showed a blotchy rim on flat studio backgrounds) -> GrowMask 16 on the crop's mask (the sampling mask: 8 left a thin line of the old colour along a draped neckline, smaller left old-colour specks at the edge) -> StringFormat "{a} Keep everything else in the picture exactly the same." -> TextEncodeQwenImage21 with the crop as image 1 (resolution 0) -> VAEEncode + SetLatentNoiseMask -> QwenImage21Cache -> KSampler 20 steps, cfg 1, euler, simple (16 looked the same as 25 on the tests) -> SplitImageWithAlpha -> Stitch Inpaint (classic, colour match 0: a tone match would pull the new colour back). Outside the piece the photo is bit-identical. RTX 5090: about 32 s per colour warm at 1.5 MP (target_megapixels 1.0 + 16 steps: 19 s, slightly softer stripes), peak 23 GB. Prompt: "Change the colour of <the piece> (Auto: the outfit) to <colour words (#hex)>. Keep its fabric, weave, folds, seams, stitching, sheen, print and shadows exactly as they are, so only the colour is new."

workflows.notes: Fuobe's Evolution on the GPU: video-segment-resample (<=81 frames @16 fps + first frame) -> qwen-image-edit-2511 takes the first frame toward the creative direction (images 2-3 = references) -> this graph -> video-concat-N -> the clip's sound. Any clip loads: VHS_LoadVideo resamples it to fps (16), keeps at most `frames` frames and cuts them to 4n+1 (Wan format), and every length in the graph is the loaded count, so a short or 30 fps clip is neither a shape error nor slow motion (Edit video sends whole clips). Unlike video-restyle-wan22-fun-vace the sampler starts from the segment itself: reference latent + VAE-encoded frames (LatentConcat on t, the shape WanVaceToVideo makes), noised to denoise = the noise level it starts from (flow matching: (1 - denoise) x clip + denoise x noise; low 0.45, medium 0.65, high 0.85). The simple scheduler with shift s reaches sigma = denoise N - steps steps into a schedule of N = round(steps x (s - (s - 1) x denoise) / denoise) steps, and the last `steps` run (Lightx2v 4-step), so the run starts within a few hundredths of any denoise from 0.02 to 1 (KSampler's floor(steps / denoise) could only make 1, 0.8, 0.67, 0.57 or 0.5 with 4 steps). Wan 2.2's high-noise expert takes only the steps at or above its switch point (sigma 0.875; ComfySwitchNode gives the first sampler the low-noise expert when the run starts below it, as all three intensities do). Control: Depth Anything 3 depth on every frame (no kept frame, no masks); the direction frame is the VACE reference. Same weights as the restyle graph.

workflows.title: FPS Boost and slow motion to an exact frame rate: interpolate by m, keep every n-th frame (core FrameInterpolate)

workflows.notes: The parity studio's FPS Boost targets (24 / 30 / 60 / 90 / 120 fps) and slow motion on the open engine. The provider picks m (multiplier, 2-16) and n (every) from the clip's own frame rate (its header) so that source fps x m / n = target x slowdown (24 -> 30 m5 n4, 24 -> 60 m5 n2, 24 -> 90 m15 n4, 24 -> 120 m5, 30 -> 60 m2, 60 -> 90 m3 n2, 60 -> 120 m2; a target the source rate is a whole multiple of (60 -> 30: m1 n2) only drops frames, and then the provider links FrameInterpolate out; other lower targets still interpolate (30 -> 24: m4 n5)). The output fps is computed in the graph from the decoded frame rate (source fps x m / (n x slowdown)); m and n need the header's rate, so the provider refuses a clip without one rather than guess. The last frame is held once more before interpolating, so the clip keeps its length (N frames become N x m + 1, about one output frame longer than the source) instead of losing a source frame. slowdown > 1 stretches the clip (2 = twice as long); the provider then drops the sound link (it would no longer match). checkpoint film_net_fp16.safetensors runs FILM (better on large motion, about 31x slower on CPU). Holds the whole interpolated clip in memory (the source frames, their copy with the last frame held, and source frames x m; the selection is a view): the provider refuses clips that need more than half the server's RAM. Frame counts and lengths, checked on CPU: 24 fps 2 s 320x180 -> 60 fps = 121 frames, 2.017 s (m 5, n 2); 25 fps 3 s with sound -> 30 fps at 2x slow motion = 181 frames, 6.03 s, no sound track; 30 fps 2 s with sound -> 24 fps = 49 frames, 2.04 s, sound kept (m 4, n 5).

workflows.notes: The kandinsky6-sr pack's Video Super Resolution template, with Fuobe's bindings: LoadVideo -> GetVideoComponents -> Kandinsky6VSRUpscale (the 2-step distilled VSR DiT from Load Diffusion Model, the K-VAE and the latent upscaler bank; tiled diffusion in latent space, overlap 0.2, NABLA attention off) -> CreateVideo with the clip's own sound (trimmed to the frames kept) -> SaveVideo. scale = params.resolution as the pack's combo ("2x", "2.25x", "4x"); upscalerScale = the bank entry it needs ("2x" for 2x and 2.25x, "4x" for 4x). The pack resamples the clip to 24 fps and keeps at most 121 frames (about 5 s): Fuobe refuses a longer clip rather than cut it. 2x and 4x need sides that are multiples of 16. Each loader lists a file only with its config.json beside it (the eight files of the SR README's manual-download table, in diffusion_models/Kandinsky-6.0-VSR-distilled2steps-5s-Diffusers/). VRAM is not published: 24 GB is an estimate (a 3.19 GB DiT, a 6.96 GB K-VAE and a 7.31 GB latent upscaler bank, loaded one stage at a time). The same model runs on fal (kandinsky-vsr).

workflows.title: World mode: one turn of a Hy-Nomas world (the opening and every turn before it, then this turn in words and a camera move, 1280x704 at 24 fps)
workflows.license: Apache-2.0 (Hy-Nomas DiT, Tencent Hunyuan; the ComfyUI files are nynxz/Hy-Nomas's conversion); PixelUMM decoder (nomas_pixelumm_vae_bf16, Tencent's fine-tune of NVIDIA PixelUMM): NVIDIA One-Way Noncommercial License (NON-COMMERCIAL research and evaluation only, per the converted weights' card); Qwen2.5-VL 7B text encoder Apache-2.0; ComfyUI-HyNomas nodes Apache-2.0
workflows.notes: Nynxz's ComfyUI-HyNomas (pinned at a89e0515) on core loaders: UNETLoader (the distilled DiT, int8 ConvRot, 8.97 GB), CLIPLoader qwen_image (qwen_2.5_vl_7b, 16.6 GB, shared with Qwen-Image), VAELoader (the PixelUMM decoder, 15.8 GB): about 25 GB of files beside the shared text encoder. The template is the pack's nomas_world example: Nomas World Prompt (perspective, style, subject, scene, action, seconds) -> Nomas World (seed, 1280x704, 8 Euler steps, window history) with a Nomas Camera Path, then Nomas World Continue for a turn (change, action, camera, seconds). Fuobe rebuilds it per run: the opening and one Continue per turn up to the one asked for, each with a key script that flies along the turn's camera move (or no camera for a still turn), then TrimVideoLatent drops the earlier turns' latents so VAE Decode -> CreateVideo 24 fps -> SaveVideo writes this turn alone. The port keeps a world in ComfyUI's memory (NOMAS_WORLD plus an int8 key/value cache in temp/nomas_history), and ComfyUI reuses the outputs of the last prompt it ran: the turns before this one have the same inputs and node ids every time, so only the new turn is generated; after another job or a restart they are generated again from the same seed. No sound (Hy-Nomas makes none). No image input: Hy-Nomas starts every world from words. Speed and VRAM are the port author's: about 21 s per 3 s turn plus about 4 s of decode per 10-latent window on an RTX 5090 at 1280x704 int8; Tencent's single-4090 configuration uses an int8 DiT and cache, an FP8 decoder and CPU offload; plan on a 24 GB card. The pack patches the core loaders' model detection (Load Diffusion Model, Load VAE) to recognise the Nomas files.

workflows.title: Qwen-Image 2.1 Head Swap (BFS head LoRA V1.1, pasted back onto the shot)
workflows.license: Qwen Research License Agreement (Qwen-Image 2.1): NON-COMMERCIAL, research and evaluation only; BFS head-swap LoRA by Alissonerdx MIT; SAM 3.1 under Meta's SAM License (commercial use allowed under its terms); GrowMaskWithBlur from ComfyUI-KJNodes (GPL-3.0 code)
workflows.notes: qwen-image-21-edit (int8, 25 steps, euler / simple, cfg 1, both pictures 2048 on the long side, resolution 0) with Alissonerdx's BFS head LoRA V1.1 at 1.0 and its training prompt ("head_swap: start with <image1> as the base image ..."). image = the shot to keep (body, pose, light, background), image2 = the head (identity, hair, eye colour): body first, head second, as V1.1 was trained; other BFS versions take other orders, so the file is pinned. V1.1 is V1 without the second-half img_mlp.gate_up modules (less skin softening, slightly weaker expression transfer); the V1.1 "alternative" file copies expression better at about 1 degree more head-pose error. Paste-back (pasteBack, on by default): SAM 3.1 finds the head ("head") on the swap and on the shot scaled to the swap's size, the two masks are joined (ImageCompositeMasked of the mask images, so old long hair goes too), grown by maskGrow and blurred by maskBlur (GrowMaskWithBlur), and only that area comes from the swap: every other pixel is the shot's, which removes Qwen 2.1's colour and detail drift over the whole picture. pasteBack false returns the whole swap (the switch is lazy, SAM does not run). No head found: the shot comes back unchanged. BFS's own workflow runs the Pruna 8-step LoRA with deis_2m (RES4LYF); this graph keeps core samplers. RTX 5090: about 130 s a photo warm, about 250 s when the models load, peak about 28 GB.
